answer: Like a river that narrows at a single inlet before reaching a wide terrace, an agent economy can force every identity through one costly gate: a stake bond. Each agent locks a refundable deposit to register; the bond is returned only after sustained honest work, and misbehavior slashes it. One real agent pays once, but a Sybil attacker must lock a fresh bond for every fake identity, so the cost of flooding the network grows linearly with each clone while honest agents get their stake back.
